problem.claim: Enable frequency-domain control over musical structure in generative music models.

contributions.claim: LatentFT combines a diffusion autoencoder with a latent-space Fourier transform to separate musical patterns by timescale and support coherent latent manipulation.
The framework enables reference-based musical variations and blends while preserving characteristics at frequencies corresponding to desired timescales.
The authors introduce isolated latent-frequency listening and report that different musical attributes occupy different regions of the latent spectrum.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present latent-space frequency-domain controls for generative music models, analogizing them to an equalizer for musical structure rather than audible timbre.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments and listening tests show improved condition adherence and quality versus baselines.
The authors report that isolated latent-frequency listening reveals different musical attributes in different spectral regions.
The authors report an intuitive, continuous latent-frequency axis for conditioning and blending.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces LatentFT for frequency-domain control in generative music.
Combines a diffusion autoencoder with a latent Fourier transform and frequency masking to organize and manipulate patterns by timescale.
Generates reference-based variations and blends while preserving selected timescale characteristics.
Reports better adherence and quality than baselines, and analyzes attribute localization across latent frequencies.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a control mechanism, an intuitive production analogy, and concrete user-facing operations such as variation and blending.

lessons.interpretation: A compact conceptual analogy can clarify how a technical representation maps to practical controls.
lessons.application: When presenting a controllable generative system, pair the representation with a familiar domain operation and name the resulting user actions.
lessons.exception: Avoid the analogy when the mapped operations or preserved properties are not explicitly demonstrated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baseline identities, evaluation metrics, dataset or test design, or the magnitude of reported improvements.
It does not provide details sufficient to assess how latent frequencies map to particular musical attributes or timescales.
